title: Grove publishes load-bearing risk parameters as placeholders while the system runs live
content:
A striking share of this chunk's safety-relevant fields are unfilled. `LIMIT_USDS_BURN` on Ethereum Mainnet (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.1.1.3.1.1.2), `LIMIT_USDC_TO_DOMAIN` on Ethereum (A...3.1.1.4), Avalanche (A...3.1.2.1) and Base (A...3.1.3.1), both off-chain parameters (A...2.1.1, A...2.1.2, A...2.2.1), and the Plasma ALM Controller version (A...2.4.2) all read that the value "will be specified in a future iteration."

The important inference is about the **document, not the system**. These limits are enforced by a deployed `ALM_RATE_LIMITS` contract whose address is given; the contract necessarily holds concrete values. What is missing is the Artifact's record of them. So the gap is documentation debt, and its cost is that the Artifact cannot be used to verify the deployment — a reader cannot check the chain against the document, because the document is silent exactly where checking would be useful.

That matters more here than elsewhere in the Atlas. The whole justification for recording addresses and limits in a governed document is that governance can then be held to them. An unspecified limit is one no proposal can be measured against and no reviewer can call a violation.

A related drift appears in versions: the ALM Controller is recorded at 1.8.0 on Ethereum, Avalanche, Base and Robinhood Chain, but 1.6.0 on Plume (A...2.5.2) and unspecified on Plasma. Whether Plume is genuinely behind or merely documented behind is not determinable from the Artifact — which is precisely the problem.
description: The USDS burn maximum, several USDC domain limits, both off-chain parameters and the Plasma controller version all read 'will be specified in a future iteration' on an Active Primitive.
